problem: Prior in-context RL scales only to a few thousand steps, mostly on non-visual tasks, so embodied agents cannot accumulate experience across many long episodes. Standard on-policy RL with a full-trial context is prohibitively sample-inefficient, and softmax attention over long, highly correlated visual histories is hard to learn.
motivation: A robot in an unseen home should use its history of completed tasks to learn the layout and object locations, and become more efficient without any parameter updates. This needs full attention over tens of thousands of visual steps, trained from reward alone. The paper observes that updating PPO several times inside one long rollout, and letting attention heads attend to nothing, makes such training feasible.
key_idea: Train a transformer in-context RL policy with PPO using 'partial updates' (multiple policy updates within one long-context rollout, with the loss applied only to the newest chunk) plus learnable per-layer Sink-KV vectors, which scales in-context adaptation to 64k steps.
insight: Ablations on ReplicaCAD show both components matter. Without partial updates the first-episode SR is 40% lower and SR gains only 5% over the trial versus 25% with them. Without any attention sink, learning is slow (<40% SR at 200M steps versus 90% with Sink-KV). In-context learning emerges only after sufficient RL training (none at 52M and 157M steps), and it generalizes to contexts 8x longer than the training context.
method: Transformer policy: a LLaMA-style causal transformer (4 layers, 8 heads, hidden 256, ~4.5M params) over the multi-episode observation history. Observations are egocentric RGB (frozen finetuned VC-1 ViT-B), proprioception and goal embeddings, concatenated; a linear head predicts actions.

Partial updates: a rollout of T steps is split into K chunks. After each T/K steps the policy is updated with PPO using context NT/K, with the loss only on the last T/K outputs. The forward pass is recomputed over the whole window, and a final full update applies the loss to all steps. Workers reset at the start of each rollout.

Sink-KV: per-layer learnable key/value vectors (s=1, adding 0.046% parameters) are prepended to K and V. Attention heads can then attend to nothing. It generalizes Softmax-One (K0V0) and sink tokens; the paper uses the Sink KV0 variant.

Episode shuffling and position encoding: after each update, older episodes in the context are shuffled and the KV cache is refreshed, as regularization. Episode index uses RoPE and within-episode position is learnable.
Efficient long-context training: KV cache storage during rollouts, FP16 rollout storage, gradient accumulation and flash-attention. Training used 4xA40 for 12 days, 1B steps, 80 workers.
Visual encoder finetuning: VC-1 is finetuned with Dice loss on a 20-class small-object presence task (21k samples) and then frozen.
Few-shot imitation: shortest-path expert demonstrations are inserted into the context with no demo training; the agent then navigates to a new object.

setting.backbone: LLaMA-style causal transformer (4 layers, 4.5M params, from scratch) + frozen finetuned VC-1 ViT-B
setting.model_size: 4.5M policy parameters (plus ViT-B VC-1 frozen encoder)
setting.training_data: Online PPO RL in HSSD scenes (37 train scenes, 12 val) with randomly placed YCB small objects (20 types); 500M steps for the baseline comparison, 1B steps for the best model; VC-1 finetuned on 21k synthetic images
setting.observation: egocentric 256x256 RGB + odometry (relative displacement) + goal object category
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, tilt camera up/down 30°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (the geodesic-distance reward is used only in training; few-shot imitation uses shortest-path expert demos in context)

numbers.eval_set_note: 10k distinct trial sequences on unseen HSSD scenes, 3 seeds; SR/SPL read at 15 episodes (8k-step context)

numbers_note: Results are mostly shown in figures; only numbers stated in the text are captured. The ablation (ReplicaCAD) and 64k-training results have no tabulated numbers. The paper does not use a standard navigation benchmark.
results: On the multi-episode small-object navigation task, ReLIC raises SR from 23% to 43% over 15 in-context episodes, while the best baseline (single-episode transformer) stays at about 22% and recurrent baselines (RL², TrXL) show no ICL. It generalizes to 32k-step contexts (>55% SR) and trains at 64k context over 175 episodes. It also does few-shot imitation (about 5% better than N self-experience episodes at N=16) and beats DPT on Darkroom and Miniworld.
limitations: ICL emerges only with a diverse training set that cannot be overfit, and requires large RL training (1B steps, 12 days on 4 A40s).
Evaluated only on a few environments (mostly one navigation task, plus Darkroom/Miniworld); no manipulation or real robot.
Results are shown mostly in plots, with a custom benchmark rather than standard ObjectNav.
